Two concrete contract defects are now clear. First, the replay optimizer is not actually PPO-clipped: after its ratio cap is reached it still applies a full log-probability gradient forever, which permits exactly this absorbing-action collapse. Second, the match shutdown records a zero-reward terminal transition instead of the realized horizon winner. I’m replacing both contracts, adding a semantic entropy floor, and making the study use the same canonical utility weights as training.

The corrected entropy-floor contract passes 39 tests. I’m running one final, shorter four-perturbation mirrored cycle from the margin checkpoint with replay/optimizer migration reset. This is evidence-driven: it tests whether removing the accidental pressure toward uniform actions closes the measured cart deficit while the 1.0-nat floor preserves robust multi-action behavior.
